transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Sasha Martinez (ProcureCorp Procurement), David Chen (ProcureCorp Security/IT), Maya Patel (ProcureCorp Legal), Evan Li (ProcureCorp Product)

Summary: procurement/legal deep-dive on MSA/DPA, SLAs and onboarding requirements. Agreed to send redline and security docs; pilot to be scheduled.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i'm jordan from redwood inference, this is priya our solutions engineer and liam on the CSM side; just to confirm names who we have?
00:08 Sasha: hi this is sasha procurement at procurecorp, we have maya from legal, david from security and evan from product on the line
00:14 Jordan: perfect, i'll run through the agenda: quick recap of the commercial terms we discussed, walk through the MSA/DPA redlines you sent, SLA targets and remedies, security questions (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and then next steps for procurement and pilot setup
00:28 Maya: sounds good, we circulated a redline version of your standard MSA and a DPA, there are a few clauses we flagged around indemnity and data residency
00:37 Priya: thanks, i'll start on the tech/security bits and jordan can take the contractual asks - on the DPA side we support data residency controls for private deployments and hosted, and we have options for contract language around data at rest encryption using customer-managed keys via KMS
00:53 David: just to be clear - we need confirmation we can use our KMS key in the private deployment and that key rotations won't cause downtime for token caches or inference state
01:05 Priya: yep, we do support bring-your-own-key for private and dedicated, and our runtime is built to honor key rotations; there is a short rekey window but we have a pattern with rolling rekeys and no KV cache invalidation when done with the documented steps - i'll include the exact ops playbook in the security pack
01:22 David: please include any limitations for hosted API too, for compliance reasons we may require dedicated or private for PHI workloads
01:30 Jordan: noted - on the MSA redlines you sent, indemnity and liability caps were flagged. our standard is a mutual cap tied to the last 12 months of fees, and we do carve out gross negligence. do you have a target cap you need?
01:44 Maya: procurement typically asks a higher cap for critical vendors; we don't expect 1:1 parity with software vendors but we'd like flexibility to negotiate to X months or a fixed number. also we asked for a 90 day SLA ramp for initial onboarding
01:57 Jordan: understood. we can propose a graduated SLA that starts at a 90 day onboarding stabilization period with reduced remedies, then moves to target SLOs after onboarding. our standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% for API availability with credits described in the SLA matrix - i'll share the detailed SLA matrix
02:12 Sasha: on pricing approvals - our finance team needs committed pricing tiers and an estimated token run-rate to greenlight a 12 month commit. can you send a pricing spreadsheet?
02:22 Jordan: yes i'll send our pricing sheet with commit discounts. we also provide batch/kv/quantization guidance that usually reduces per-token cost - priya will annotate expected savings based on your typical requests
02:35 Evan: for our pilot we'll run LLM-based summarization across PHI-adjacent documents; we need to know whether hosted is allowed or if we must use private. we also need integration notes for SSO and RBAC so only certain users can call endpoints
02:50 Priya: for PHI we usually recommend Dedicated or Private; we can provision a private deployment in your VPC or a private-hosted plane. SSO/SAML and SCIM for RBAC are supported, and we have a guide. i'll put the SSO playbook in the dropbox link
03:07 David: audit logs - we need per-request audit trails for 2 years, are those available?
03:12 Priya: yes audit logs are available, retention is configurable; long-term retention may be an add-on. logs include request metadata and tokens are not stored in plaintext, we can redact inputs on request - will include audit retention costs in the security pack
03:28 Maya: on the DPA, our main concern was subprocessors and subcontractor flow-down. can you confirm how you manage third-party inference providers or cloud providers?
03:38 Jordan: our DPA lists subprocessors; we can provide a current list and a 30-day notice for changes. for private deployments we can restrict subprocessors since customer control plane is limited. i'll send the latest subprocessors list and SOC2 report
03:53 Sasha: procurement process - we need to understand sign-off cadence: legal (maya), security (david) and finance (sasha) then exec approval. typical timeline is 2-3 weeks after redline sign-off, can you compress onboarding?
04:08 Liam: from a CSM/onboarding perspective we can run concurrent activities: legal review can happen in parallel with pilot and technical integration. typical pilot + onboarding to production is 4-6 weeks depending on infra provisioning
04:22 Evan: will the pilot require dedicated GPUs or can we run on hosted for eval?
04:28 Priya: for evaluation we can spin up hosted sandbox with rate limits and a small dedicated test cluster if you want more realistic latency/throughput. for PHI we recommend a private test cluster in your VPC to mimic production
04:42 Maya: pricing sensitivity - if we sign a 12 month commit what SLAs are guaranteed? what are the remedies?
04:49 Jordan: guaranteed SLOs and remedies are enumerated in the SLA matrix - credits based on downtime; for higher SLAs we can discuss financial credits or service credits. we'll attach the matrix and examples from similar customers
04:59 David: on encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between our services and your endpoints?
05:05 Priya: yes we support mTLS and client certs, plus token-based auth. i'll include the mTLS cert rotation schedule and any integration caveats
05:17 Sasha: one more: data residency - we need EU data stored in eu-region only for certain subsets; does your hosted offering allow region pinning?
05:27 Jordan: yes region pinning is supported at the tenant level for hosted and is default for private. we'll note residency options in the DPA and deployment appendix
05:35 Maya: we had a few specific contract asks: 1) ability to terminate for convenience with 90 days, 2) audit rights for our security team, 3) clarification on incident notification windows
05:48 Jordan: 1) termination for convenience is negotiable at the enterprise tier, can follow contract terms; 2) audit rights we can provide SOC2 and limited on-site audits under NDA, we'll clarify the scope; 3) incident notifications: we commit to T-1 hour initial notification for Sev1s with a follow-up timeline in the SLA pack
06:05 David: will you provide an ATO package or evidence for our compliance cycle?
06:10 Priya: we can provide SOC2 report, encryption attestations, penetration test summary and an architecture diagram for ATO efforts - we'll share that in the security pack link after the call
06:21 Jordan: ok real quick recap of immediate artifacts we'll send: updated DPA with highlights, SLA matrix, pricing spreadsheet with commit tiers, security pack (SOC2, pen test summary, KMS docs, SSO guide), subprocessors list and pilot onboarding checklist
06:36 Sasha: good. timeline - we'll aim to have internal legal review by 9/24 and procurement sign-off by 9/30 if all looks good
06:45 Jordan: that's reasonable. will you be the owner for the procurement timeline?
06:48 Sasha: yes i'll own procurement timeline and coordinate with maya and david
06:52 Jordan: great, priya will reach out to schedule the SE-led pilot for 9/22 at a tentative time; liam will follow up with onboarding steps and a kickoff doc
06:59 Maya: one last question - any special SOC or compliance add-ons cost?
07:04 Jordan: audit log long-term retention and private deployment network costs are usually add-ons; i'll call those out in the pricing sheet so you can see line items
07:16 Evan: thanks all, we'll look for the links and coordinate schedules
07:20 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts by EOD tomorrow and set the pilot invite. end call

End transcript.
